title: Persistent and compartmentalized T cell immunity in ALS
desc: In ALS, persistent T cell responses relate to disease outcome differently in blood than in cerebrospinal fluid, with both intrathecal antigen presentation and cytomegalovirus-specific immunity linked to worse clinical outcomes. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a fatal neurodegenerative disease increasingly linked to T cell responses, although the mechanisms driving T cell activation and disease progression remain unclear. Here we used single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing, longitudinal immune profiling and imaging flow cytometry to identify long-lived intrathecal clonotypes and antigen-presenting cell–T cell complexes displaying features of immunological synapse formation, consistent with intrathecal antigen presentation. Higher frequencies of CD4^+ effector, CD4^+ regulatory and CD8^+ T cells in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) were associated with slower disease progression, whereas increased circulating CD4^+ effector and regulatory T cells were associated with faster progression. T cell clonotypes shared between blood and CSF exhibited distinct transcriptional states. Finally, frequencies of cytomegalovirus-specific T cells in CSF and anticytomegalovirus serum antibodies were correlated with faster progression and shorter survival in sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. These findings reveal compartmentalized immune dynamics, largely contrasting protective intrathecal responses with harmful systemic activation.

title: Automation Bias and Deskilling in Radiology AI: A Confidence-stratified Triage Model for Workflow Integration.
desc: [Radiology. Artificial intelligence] Radiology is adopting artificial intelligence (AI) faster than it is studying what AI does to radiologists' perceptual expertise and interpretive skill. The question has partly shifted from whether these tools perform well on benchmark tasks to what happens to clinical judgment when use of these tools becomes routine. Two risks accompany this transition: automation bias, the tendency to follow AI suggestions without adequate scrutiny, and deskilling, the erosion of perceptual and interpretive ability through disuse, typically revealed when AI support is withdrawn. Incorrect AI output degrades accuracy regardless of experience, the benefit of assistance varies unpredictably across readers and tasks, and performance falls after AI withdrawal; neither risk has been studied longitudinally in radiology. A confidence-stratified triage model is proposed in which calibrated AI confidence, not findings alone, routes cases to low-, intermediate-, or high-confidence streams: output withheld until independent reading, shown with uncertainty signals and a checklist, or shown with random blinded audit. Demonstrated local confidence calibration is a precondition for deployment, and stream thresholds and audit rates should be weighted by task and potential clinical harm, not error probability alone. Rather than applying one workflow to every case, the model redistributes radiologist attention to where AI error is most likely and most consequential, operationalizing four principles: keeping the radiologist in the decision loop, making AI uncertainty visible, inserting targeted cognitive friction, and governing the human-AI interaction as a system. A research agenda to determine whether these countermeasures reduce automation bias and skill erosion in practice is also proposed.

title: A physics-informed peripheral hemodynamic digital twin for personalized estimation of arterial stiffness
desc: Arterial stiffness, commonly assessed by pulse wave velocity (PWV), is an important biomarker of cardiovascular risk, yet conventional PWV measurements require dual-site recordings that limit scalability in clinical settings. Here we introduce a physics-informed peripheral hemodynamic digital twin framework for estimating central-brachial arterial stiffness from a single brachial pressure waveform. Using our laboratory-developed cuff device, high-resolution brachial pulse waveforms were collected in a cohort of 118 subjects. The digital twin then personalizes a reduced-order wave propagation model through PDE-constrained optimization, generating a compact parameter space that encodes ventricular–vascular characteristics relevant to stiffness. Incorporating digital-twin-derived parameters improved PWV estimation on a blind test cohort ( r = 0.67, RMSE = 1.12 m/s) compared with a baseline model using only age and blood pressure ( r = 0.22, RMSE = 1.90 m/s). These results indicate that physics-informed digital twins can enable scalable, noninvasive assessment of vascular aging from accessible peripheral waveforms.

title: Moving beyond overconfidence: A clinical roadmap for integrating uncertainty-aware AI models into medical workflows
desc: Luo et al. review uncertainty quantification in medical AI from a clinical perspective and propose a practical roadmap for translating uncertainty estimates into meaningful action. They highlight the need to validate uncertainty against clinically relevant errors and embed its use within real-world workflows and governance.

title: Artificial intelligence and anti-cancer drugs: advancing discovery, personalization, and precision oncology.
desc: [Frontiers in oncology] Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monitoring. A key focus is on integrating AI with multi-omics data, including proteomics, genomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics, to support precision oncology and personalized treatments. We address important validation challenges, like model interpretability, data quality, and regulatory issues that must be solved before AI can be widely used in clinics. By summarizing current evidence and targeting research gaps, this review offers a clear view of how AI is enhancing the discovery, personalization, and validation of anticancer treatments.

title: AI-Assisted Differentiation of Autoimmune Pancreatitis and Pancreatic Cancer Using EUS: A Multicenter Ambispective Study
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Ruijin Hospital; conditions: Autoimmune Pancreatitis, Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC); type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 690; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Focal autoimmune pancreatitis (f-AIP) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibit substantial overlap in clinical manifestations and imaging features, posing a major diagnostic challenge in pancreatic diseases. Given the marked differences in treatment strategies and prognosis, accurate differentiation is essential to avoid unnecessary surgery and ensure timely initiation of anticancer treatment. This study aims to collect endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) images from patients with confirmed f-AIP or PDAC across multiple centers, using a previously established multicenter database. Data collected before January 2026 will be used to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) model based on EUS radiomics for differential diagnosis. Subsequently, prospectively collected data from participating centers from 2026 onward will be used for model testing and validation. The diagnostic performance of the model will be evaluated and compared with that of endoscopists with different levels of experience. Furthermore, this study will investigate the clinical value of interpretable radiomic features, with particular emphasis on challenging diagnostic scenarios, including IgG4-negative AIP, AIP with elevated carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) levels, and PDAC with imaging features resembling those of AIP. The ultimate goal is to provide a reliable tool for accurate, noninvasive preoperative differential diagnosis while promoting the standardization of multicenter AIP databases and the sharing and utilization of imaging data resources.

title: MoveBench: A Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Sports and Health Coaching
desc: Despite rapid advances in large language models (LLMs), their deployment in the sports and health domain remains high-risk due to the absence of domain-specific evaluation benchmarks. Existing general-purpose benchmarks (e.g., MMLU and HELM) primarily assess broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities, but fail to capture critical domain requirements such as exercise safety, physiological appropriateness, personalization, and actionable coaching quality. This gap is particularly concerning in fitness and health applications, where incorrect or unsafe recommendations can lead to physical harm. To address this limitation, we introduce MoveBench, the first comprehensive benchmarking framework specifically designed for evaluating LLMs in sports and health coaching. The proposed benchmark integrates heterogeneous task formats, including multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and open-ended question answering (OpenQA), grounded in real-world user scenarios and paired with structured rubrics emphasizing safety compliance, scientific validity, and training logic. Through large-scale evaluation of 15 diverse LLMs on 809 questions with 5,012 rubric-level criteria, our results reveal substantial performance variability, particularly in safety awareness, structured program design, and personalization capability, highlighting a critical gap between knowing and doing. Our work establishes a foundational evaluation standard for sports and health LLM applications and provides a reproducible framework for advancing safe, reliable, and context-aware AI-driven coaching systems. Open resources are available at https://github.com/SatoSakula/MoveBench.

title: Richer database context improves LLM-generated EHR phenotyping algorithms
desc: Objective: To evaluate large language model (LLM) generation of type 2 diabetes (T2DM) phenotyping SQL and the effect of database implementation context. Materials and Methods: Eight publicly accessible LLM-based systems generated SQL under progressively richer prompts using synthetic and University of North Carolina (UNC) Health electronic health record (EHR) data, both based on the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) model. Outputs were compared with the Electronic Medical Records and Genomics (eMERGE) T2DM reference phenotype using SQL executability, F1, positive predictive value (PPV), and recall. Results: Fewer than 55% of limited-context synthetic outputs and no limited-context UNC EHR outputs executed without modification. Detailed codebooks (L3) increased executability to 81.3% in synthetic OMOP and 100% in UNC EHR; adding sample rows (L4) increased synthetic executability to 100%. Limited-context recall was as low as 0.01, whereas high-context outputs achieved recall [≥]0.99 at synthetic L4 and >0.90 at UNC L3, although UNC PPV remained substantially lower than recall. At the highest available context levels, Beta F1 ranged from 0.72-0.99 in synthetic OMOP and 0.57-0.68 in UNC EHR; all UNC models exceeded the diagnosis-code baseline (F1=0.54). The top synthetic performer fell from F1=0.99 to 0.64 on UNC EHR. Discussion: Richer database context was associated with more consistent SQL executability and recall, while model rankings varied across datasets. Conclusion: LLMs can generate clinically meaningful T2DM phenotyping SQL when provided with sufficient database context, but limited PPV in real-world data underscores the need for local validation.

title: Building virtual cell dynamics that evolve with biological measurements
desc: Virtual cell models built from single-cell measurements need to predict how cells change over time, but new biological measurements often reveal dynamical relationships that existing models cannot express. Translating such measurements into dynamics therefore requires deciding what biological relation should be modeled, where it should enter the formulation and how its recovery should be validated. Here we present CellCompass, an agentic AI system that couples a scientific agent with an extensible dynamical engine for modeling state transitions and population change, along with fate and molecular readout. CellCompass reuses existing formulations when sufficient and designs, implements and refines new ones when experimental measurements introduce additional constraints. To assess this capability, we developed DynBench100, a benchmark of 100 simulated single-cell time-course scenarios with hidden dynamical ground truth. CellCompass achieved the highest aggregate performance among the tested general-purpose and biomedical agents across six dynamical tasks. Across four real single-cell studies, it retained an existing velocity-growth model to reconstruct context-dependent epithelial-mesenchymal transition and developed three new dynamical formulations for distinct experimental measurements. In drug-response data, incorporating metabolic RNA labeling reduced pulse-control identifiability error by 31.1%, revealing staged response programs and generating testable predictions for perturbing a candidate adaptive program. In hematopoietic lineage tracing, incorporating clonal barcodes improved clone-fate agreement by 54% over the strongest dynamical baseline, identifying early lineage priming among transcriptionally similar progenitors. Finally, in time-resolved CITE-seq data, CellCompass reduced future surface-protein distribution error by 13.2% for RNA-initialized trajectories, uncovering lineage-specific temporal offsets between transcriptional and protein programs. Together, CellCompass provides a framework in which virtual-cell dynamics can expand with the biological measurements used to constrain them.

Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial
desc: The phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE study is investigating perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy (AEGEAN regimen) in resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer and chemoradiotherapy (CRT) followed by consolidation durvalumab (PACIFIC regimen) in patients who become unresectable after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy guided by multidisciplinary team assessments during the neoadjuvant period. The primary endpoint was the overall resection rate (descriptive with no formal hypothesis testing). Secondary endpoints included event-free survival, progression-free survival, pathological complete response rate (resectable patients cohort), circulating tumor DNA clearance between baseline and presurgery/pre-CRT and safety. Overall, 142 patients received neoadjuvant treatment; 64.8% and 35.2% were deemed resectable and borderline resectable at baseline, respectively. The overall resection rate (95% confidence interval) was 74.6% (66.7‒81.6) in a population that included more than one-third of patients with borderline resectable disease. R0 resection rate was 96.2% (90.6‒99.0) in those who underwent surgery. Overall, 131 (92.3%) patients had surgery ( n = 106) or CRT ( n = 25) after neoadjuvant treatment, and 117 (82.4%) patients received adjuvant ( n = 94) or consolidation ( n = 23) durvalumab. During adjuvant or consolidation durvalumab, maximum grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 7.4% of resected patients and 17.4% of CRT-treated patients, with 8.5% and 13.0% discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. This multidisciplinary team-guided approach was feasible and enabled delivery of curative-intent treatment (surgery or CRT), followed by durvalumab in most patients, and demonstrated encouraging preliminary efficacy with a manageable adjuvant or consolidation safety profile that was consistent with prior studies. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05925530 . As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In the global phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial, neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer, followed by multidisciplinary reassessment, enabled surgery in most patients, leading to encouraging pathological complete response rates, and no additional safety concerns were reported when patients with unresectable tumors continued with chemoradiotherapy and consolidative durvalumab.

title: Clinical Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Chronic Hepatitis B.
source: PubMed · Journal of gastroenterology and hepatology
desc: [Journal of gastroenterology and hepatology] Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) burdens the healthcare system, affecting millions of individuals worldwide with a potential progression to complications such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The World Health Organization launched the chronic viral hepatitis elimination plan which aimed to eliminate chronic hepatitis B virus by 2030, yet the goal has seemed to be far from reach with the remaining few years owing to different hurdles ranging from screening strategy and diagnosis to risk stratification for antiviral treatment and HCC surveillance. To refine the management of CHB, previous studies focused on identifying the at-risk populations and predictors for adverse outcomes using conventional statistical methods. With the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI), there is further room to improve different aspects of screening and management. For instance, generative AI, such as large language models (LLMs), has been proven to have the ability to answer different clinical questions, assisting patients' and physicians' decision on various clinical scenarios. Different machine learning and deep learning models have also been developed to assess for liver fibrosis, as well as to aid segmentation of liver structures and detection of focal liver lesions through various imaging modalities. While different AI models have shown superior performance compared to those developed through traditional statistical models, the lack of standardized datasets in training cohorts and the unresolved concerns of hallucination of false information in LLMs pose challenges on applying AI in the current management of CHB, in which further studies are required to adopt AI into daily clinical practice.

title: Recombinant Human Prourokinase for Acute Ischemic Stroke in the Extended Window Selected by CT-Based Artificial Intelligence
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, School of Medicine; conditions: Acute Ischemic Stroke; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: PHASE3; enrollment: 826; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This multicenter, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intravenous recombinant human prourokinase (rhPro-UK) in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated more than 4.5 hours and up to 24 hours after stroke onset, selected using a noncontrast computed tomography-based artificial intelligence (CT-AI) tissue-window algorithm. A total of 826 participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intravenous rhPro-UK or matching placebo, in addition to guideline-recommended standard stroke care. The primary outcome is the proportion of participants achieving a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-1 at 90 ± 7 days. Secondary outcomes include functional outcomes, changes in neurological deficits, early neurological improvement at 24 hours and 7 days, and tissue reperfusion at 24-48 hours. Safety outcomes include symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, parenchymal hematoma, all-cause mortality, and serious systemic bleeding.

title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
desc: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant scattering has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models. We leverage a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model to analyze polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) from molecular thin films. This new analysis establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states as a function of depth with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit via locking energy and polarization through the optical model. From our analysis, we discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from the interface, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics and contradicting hypotheses of substrate patterning. This nondestructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final state opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.

title: EM-BENCH: A Reproducible Framework for Benchmarking Guideline-Concordant Clinical Decision Making in Large Language Models
desc: Background Physicians increasingly use artificial intelligence tools to support clinical work, yet there is no accepted standard for measuring the competency of large language models (LLMs) in clinical decision support. We developed EM-BENCH, a physician-validated, deterministically scored benchmark for evaluating whether models reliably apply the American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) guidelines to clinical decisions. Methods EM-BENCH comprises 210 binary clinical vignettes covering all 70 critical questions across 25 ACEP clinical policies. We evaluated 149 LLM configurations representing 79 base models using prespecified answers and deterministic scoring. Each vignette had a prespecified correct answer to a binary yes-or-no question based on an ACEP recommendation. We examined associations between accuracy and model access tier (closed-access vs. open-weight models), model size, release date, clinical policy, recommendation evidence level, and reasoning settings. Results No configuration achieved complete guideline concordance. The highest performing configuration answered 207 of 210 vignettes correctly (98.6%). Closed-access models outperformed open-weight models (median accuracy, 91% vs. 63%; Hodges-Lehmann location shift, 26 percentage points; 99% CI, 20 to 33; adjusted P<0.001). Among open-weight model families, a 10-fold increase in parameter count was associated with a 14-percentage-point increase in accuracy (99% CI, 7.7 to 20; adjusted P<0.001). Across all models, accuracy increased by 8.9 percentage points per release year (99% CI, 3.6 to 14; adjusted P<0.001). Neither enabling a thinking mode (pseudomedian change, 0.95 percentage points; 99% CI, -2.6 to 3.1; adjusted P=1.00) nor high versus low reasoning effort (0.91 percentage points; 99% CI, -0.69 to 3.1; adjusted P=0.56) consistently improved accuracy. Conclusions Contemporary LLMs showed improving but incomplete ability to apply ACEP guidelines. Concordance varied markedly across models and was associated with access tier, size, and release recency, while additional inference-time reasoning offered inconsistent benefit. Specialty-specific, physician-validated benchmarks may provide a reproducible assessment of LLMs' ability to make guideline-concordant clinical decisions.

title: Verifiable Agentic Science on Public Infrastructure
desc: Autonomous artificial intelligence agents are transforming the practice of science. Across every discipline, researchers are handing data analysis to coding agents that can design and execute complex studies from a single prompt. Yet this revolution carries a threat. When agents improvise in local environments, they leave no verifiable record, ultimately risking a wave of irreproducible science. Solving this crisis requires moving agentic science onto public infrastructure where every action leaves an examinable trail. Here we connect autonomous coding agents to shared computing resources, turning ephemeral prompts into auditable scientific records. After showing that 30 unguided local agents splinter into 18 incompatible pipelines on the same dataset, we conduct an agentic reproduction and discovery study on a large scale---reproducing a large, diverse array of studies with every workflow, history, and intermediate dataset publicly accessible. This complete provenance trail exposes unstated modeling choices, reference mismatches, and subsampled tutorial inputs in published studies, and establishes a new foundation where human scientists can understand, steer, and trust AI-driven discovery.

title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity
desc: This Review examines the cellular, organ-level and whole-body differences between metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity, as well as variations in response to weight loss—with the goal of improving strategies for preventing and treating obesity-related metabolic disorders. Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. A better understanding of the differences between metabolically divergent groups and the physiological responses to weight loss can help identify the factors responsible for the link between excess adiposity and metabolic dysfunction and disease.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Cataract Surgery: A Review of Preoperative, Intraoperative and Postoperative Applications.
desc: [Clinical & experimental ophthalmology] Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology in the fields of medicine and ophthalmology. Recent advances in machine learning, deep learning and convolutional neural networks have significantly improved cataract detection and grading, intraocular lens power calculations, surgical decision-making, risk prediction and patient education. Intraoperative AI-assisted surgical phase recognition, workflow analysis, real-time guidance, robotic technologies and femtosecond laser integration can improve surgical precision, efficiency and safety. AI has shown promise in predicting visual outcomes, detecting postoperative complications and facilitating telemedicine follow-up. Though challenges with AI include transparency, data diversity, regulatory oversight and clinical validation, continued advances are expected to further personalise cataract surgery, support clinical decision-making, optimise surgical performance and improve patient outcomes. This narrative summarises the current and emerging applications of AI in preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative management of cataracts.

title: Virtual Follow-up Prediction of Subsolid Pulmonary Nodules: A Prospective Silent Reader Study
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology; conditions: Pulmonary Subsolid Nodules, Ground-Glass Nodules; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 200; status: COMPLETED] The goal of this prospective, non-interventional study is to evaluate the predictive performance and potential clinical utility of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based virtual follow-up framework for incidentally detected pulmonary subsolid nodules (SSNs), including pure ground-glass and part-solid nodules. The main questions it aims to answer are: 1. Can the AI model accurately predict future CT appearances, quantitative growth characteristics, and morphological progression of pulmonary SSNs at specified follow-up intervals? 2. Does AI-assisted virtual follow-up improve radiologists' assessment of nodule progression and simulated surveillance management decisions compared with assessment without AI assistance? Researchers will compare radiologists' assessments with and without access to AI-generated future CT images and quantitative predictions. An additional reader evaluation will examine whether generated future images provide incremental value beyond quantitative predictions alone. Participants will undergo clinically indicated CT examinations and receive routine care according to standard clinical practice. The research team will: * Collect previously acquired CT images and clinical information. * Generate and lock AI predictions before the corresponding follow-up CT examinations occur. * Obtain and lock radiologists' assessments and simulated management recommendations before actual follow-up outcomes become available. * Compare predicted nodule progression with observed follow-up CT findings. AI predictions and research-related reader assessments will not be disclosed to treating clinicians or used to alter patients' actual surveillance or treatment decisions.

title: VascFlux-GEO: Comparator selection and auditability in vascular transcriptome module prediction
desc: Background: Mathematical coupling and comparator selection are established concerns when a transcriptome response is defined as follow-up minus baseline. We assessed whether apparent within-cohort improvement survives matched constant-follow-up and scalar-shrinkage controls, and whether specified evaluation faults are detectable in an auditable vascular transcriptome benchmark. Results: Using eight frozen modules, 72 rosuvastatin pairs, 14 peripheral artery disease pairs, 20 repeated subject-held-out five-fold partitions, and 5,000 subject bootstrap draws of fixed losses, we compared 15 explicit specifications. Supporting post hoc analyses included 800 known-truth training/test simulations, annotation and input-ablation sensitivities, complete-tuning integrity checks, and an independent-source cross-sectional artery description. In GSE86216, nested follow-up ridge had lower observed repeated-CV mean absolute error than mean follow-up, 0.3280 versus 0.3405 (difference 0.0126; descriptive central 95% percentile range 0.0033-0.0224), while scalar shrinkage had lower observed error (0.3256). These ranges have no validated coverage guarantee. No full-matrix advantage was established; equivalence was not tested. In peripheral artery disease, nested ridge (0.3449) had slightly higher observed MAE than the median follow-up comparator (0.3409), and no advantage was established. Simulations illustrated how mean follow-up can outperform mean change without temporal signal, while the GSE281841 histological stenosis-grade description remained limited by anatomical imbalance, unconfirmed participant identity and an unresolved sample-count discrepancy. Conclusions: These retrospective, nonconfirmatory comparisons show modestly lower observed within-cohort error than constant-follow-up controls in one cohort, without established full-matrix advantage. They do not partition prediction into mathematical, technical and biological components. Independent longitudinal validation and clinical utility remain unestablished.

title: PepPr: De Novo peptide sequencing with peptide priors
desc: Mass spectrometry-based peptide sequencing underpins proteomics. Database search confines to predefined candidates, whereas de novo peptide sequencing (DNPS) struggles with incomplete spectra. Existing hybrid methods use databases only for post hoc correction or retrieve previously identified spectra to guide decoding. We instead combine DNPS with a peptide prior: a language model fitted to a reference proteome, tolerating variants yet uncertain on strongly divergent sequences. Relative to prior-free DNPS, our implementation, PepPr, improved reference peptide identification and improved rather than suppressed variant identification. Using a related proteome as prior, it matched or outperformed homology-driven database search, and its gain over prior-free DNPS grew with relatedness. In antibody sequencing, it improved recovery of peptides spanning the variable-constant boundary, deamidation calls, and assembly, while preserving recall of hypervariable regions inaccessible to database search. Peptide priors thus bring reference knowledge into DNPS without limiting discovery.

title: Innovation and AI in Endourology: An Overview from EAU Endourology.
desc: [Current urology reports] Advancements in technology have been at the heart of endourology for decades. With the introduction of new and novel technologies, endourology is rapidly changing. This review aims to address the recent innovations and technological advances in endourology by addressing four different areas where tangible outcome improvements are being seen: (1) diagnostic and detection methods; (2) intraoperative optimisation and procedural automation; (3) prediction of treatment outcomes; and (4) the use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for patients' education and monitoring. AI applications in endourology consistently demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy, with stone detection rates exceeding 95% across imaging modalities. Emerging tools include non-invasive analysis of stone composition and real-time intraoperative segmentation. Intraoperative improvements involve augmented reality-guided renal access, which has reduced puncture times, fluoroscopy exposure, and complications. New instruments, such as flexible, navigable suction devices (FANS) and intrarenal pressure (IRP) and temperature (IRT) monitoring systems, bring the field closer to achieving the endourological quadrifecta. Machine learning models trained on multicentre data can predict perioperative risks and personalise treatment, demonstrating similar effectiveness in managing stone disease. Additionally, generative AI and large language models are increasingly used for clinical documentation, patient communication, and outpatient workflows. However, concerns about hallucination, data privacy, and the need for human oversight remain significant in this growing area. Innovation, technology, and AI in endourology are advancing rapidly, introducing new ideas that are integrated into surgical procedures. These innovations offer numerous benefits to patients at various stages of treatment, leading to improved surgical results. Although combining these technologies can potentially maximise patient benefits, a careful and selective approach should be adopted, accompanied by thorough assessments before implementing these new innovations.

title: MYTP01 for Immune-Mediated Diseases
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Zhejiang Provincial People's Hospital; conditions: IgA Nephropathy, Kidney Transplant Recipients, Lupus Nephritis, Primary Membranous Nephropathy, ANCA-associated Vasculitis; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 160; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] The goal of this study is to evaluate whether MYTP01, a traditional Chinese herbal formula developed by clinical experts with the assistance of artificial intelligence (AI), is effective and safe as an additional treatment for immune-mediated diseases (post-kidney transplantation, IgA nephropathy, etc.). The study also aims to explore whether MYTP01 may provide therapeutic benefits across these conditions by regulating shared immune and inflammatory processes. The main questions this study aims to answer are: * Does MYTP01 provide clinical benefits and remain safe when used as an additional treatment for immune-mediated conditions? * Does MYTP01 help regulate immune balance and inflammatory responses across immune-mediated disease populations? Researchers will compare MYTP01 with a matching placebo, with both treatments given in addition to standard medical care, to evaluate clinical efficacy, safety, and potential immunomodulatory effects across immune-mediated conditions. Participants will: * Be enrolled in a disease-specific cohort based on their clinical condition. * Be randomly assigned to receive either MYTP01 or placebo in addition to their usual medical treatment. * Take the assigned study treatment twice daily for 8 weeks. * Attend follow-up visits approximately once a month during a 12-week study period. * Undergo clinical assessments, blood and urine tests, and evaluations of immune function and possible side effects.

title: Large language models detect methodological errors that human peer review misses in clinical trials
desc: Peer review is the principal quality control of published research, but methodological errors can go undetected. In an earlier experiment with errors inserted into three reports of randomized clinical trials, untrained human reviewers achieved a mean major-error detection score of 27%. Here, we tested whether 15 large language models (LLMs), including four open-weight models, detect the same errors. Their major-error detection scores ranged from 53% to 96%. To reduce the risk of memorization, we repeated the test on three clinical trials published in 2026. Scores ranged from 51% to 99%, and from 66% to 87% for the open-weight models. Notably, LLMs still flagged 2% to 29% of the error types in control reports without inserted errors, most often conclusions not supported by the results and missing reasons why screened patients were not enrolled. Across the 12 models, mean review times ranged from 1.4 to 16.3 minutes. Opus 5.5 achieved the highest major-error detection score (99%), while GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna offered cost-effective alternatives with scores of 92% and 87%, respectively. Together, these tests provide a benchmark for specialized review models and suggest that relying on human peer review alone may leave avoidable methodological errors undetected.

title: Perturbation-based propagation of bacterial composition uncertainty improves robustness and reproducibility of microbiome differential abundance analysis.
desc: Differential abundance (DA) analysis remains the analytical bottleneck of microbiome science; despite dozens of available methods, results remain poorly reproducible across tools, datasets, and study designs. Three intertwined challenges drive this failure: compositional data structure, stochastic count uncertainty, and complex experimental design; yet no existing method addresses all three simultaneously. Here, we introduce PARALLAX (Perturbation-based Assessment of Robustness Across Latent Logical Axes), a unified DA framework that resolves this gap by propagating compositional uncertainty through per-replicate linear mixed modeling across a structured scale perturbation grid, then summarizes inference through two stability-based metrics: Ppost (effect consistency across Monte Carlo replicates) and Rscale (robustness to scale perturbation). PARALLAX retains uncertainty through the complete inferential pipeline while natively supporting repeated measures and multifactorial designs. Under repeated subsampling, PARALLAX identified fully stable DA taxa in 14.4% of cases, versus 1.7% and 0% for comparators. We applied PARALLAX to two independent longitudinal shotgun metagenomic datasets from mechanistically distinct mouse models: Gulf War toxicant exposure and repetitive head trauma. In both, PARALLAX resolved robust, sex-specific, and time-dependent genus-level shifts while accommodating repeated measures and multifactorial design, tasks that challenged both comparator frameworks. PARALLAX is released as an open-source, AI-compatible R workflow, lowering the barrier to rigorous microbiome DA analysis across complex study designs.

title: The use of biological age and artificial intelligence in health care.
desc: [npj aging] This commentary highlights the age illusion and advocates integrating biological age and artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance clinical precision in health care. By synthesizing geroscience and machine learning, practitioners and scientists can effectively bridge the gap between experimental biomarkers and personalized medicine and longevity care. This contribution is timely as the importance of biological age and predictive analytics offer transformative potential for diagnostics while necessitating a focus on modern medical systems. This article aims to elucidate how AI accelerates the clinical implementation of biological age rather than current chronological age in precision medicine.

title: Vision-Language-Based Large-Scale Model for Emergency Screening
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: The First Hospital of Jilin University; conditions: Acute Thoraco-Abdominal Emergency Lesions; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 640; status: RECRUITING] This is a single-center, prospective, stratified 1:1 parallel-group randomized superiority diagnostic trial at The First Hospital of Jilin University. Eligible emergency patients aged ≥18 who received routine thoraco-abdominal non-contrast CT were randomly assigned to two groups. The experimental group adopted a self-developed vision-language large model (powER) for auxiliary CT interpretation, while the control group received standard radiological reading without AI assistance. All participants completed standardized 60-day clinical follow-up to obtain clinical gold-standard outcomes. The primary objective is to compare the diagnostic performance of the AI model versus conventional radiology interpretation for multiple acute thoraco-abdominal emergency lesions.

title: Artificial intelligence in digital implant dentistry: current applications, clinical translation, and future directions.
desc: [Odontology] Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly expanded across digital implant dentistry, with applications ranging from diagnosis and treatment planning to surgical execution, prosthetic rehabilitation, outcome prediction, and biomechanical optimization. However, the clinical readiness and translational value of many proposed AI systems remain uncertain. This comprehensive state-of-the-art narrative review aims to provide an integrated overview of AI applications throughout the implant workflow while critically evaluating current evidence, methodological limitations, and challenges to clinical implementation. A comprehensive narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by Google Scholar and manual reference screening. The review was prepared according to SANRA recommendations. AI has demonstrated promising performance in automated image analysis, implant planning, computer-assisted surgery, prosthetic workflows, implant identification, peri-implant disease detection, predictive modelling, and biomechanical optimization. Nevertheless, most available evidence is derived from retrospective studies, simulation-based investigations, or single-center datasets. Limited external validation, heterogeneity in study design, and insufficient prospective clinical evidence continue to restrict widespread clinical adoption. Furthermore, improvements in technical performance do not necessarily translate into superior patient-centered outcomes. AI has the potential to enhance efficiency, consistency, and clinical decision support throughout the implant workflow. However, current evidence supports its role primarily as an adjunctive tool rather than an autonomous clinical system. Future progress will depend on robust validation, standardized reporting, explainable AI frameworks, and prospective clinical studies demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient outcomes. Clinical Relevance Statement: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in the digital implant workflow, from radiographic analysis and virtual patient construction to computer-assisted surgery, prosthetic design, and outcome prediction. This review helps clinicians distinguish the AI-specific components of these technologies from conventional digital tools, identify which applications are supported by clinical evidence versus those that remain experimental, and understand the current limitations regarding validation, generali

title: Large Language Model Support for CTEPH Differential Diagnosis
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: China-Japan Friendship Hospital; conditions: Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension (CTEPH), Acute Pulmonary Embolism (PE), Pulmonary Artery Sarcoma; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 60; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate whether a locked large language model (LLM)-based clinical decision support system improves the differential diagnosis of pulmonary artery filling defects among physicians who do not specialize in pulmonary vascular diseases. Participants will evaluate 30 de-identified clinical cases involving chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH), acute pulmonary embolism (PE), and pulmonary artery sarcoma (PAS), with or without LLM assistance. The primary outcome is sensitivity for identifying CTEPH, while secondary outcomes include overall diagnostic accuracy, time to diagnosis, appropriateness of referral recommendations, and AI-related diagnostic errors.

title: Artificial intelligence readiness profiles associated with critical thinking among nursing interns: A latent profile analysis.
desc: [Nurse education today] To identify distinct profiles of artificial intelligence (AI) readiness among nursing interns, to explore the relationship between these profiles and critical thinking ability, and to examine the factors associated with profile membership. The integration of AI into healthcare and nursing education necessitates that nursing students develop AI readiness. Critical thinking is a core competency for clinical decision-making and professional practice. Understanding how AI readiness profiles relate to critical thinking can inform tailored educational interventions. A cross-sectional survey study. A total of 458 nursing interns were recruited via convenience sampling from a teaching hospital in China. Data were collected using the Medical Artificial Intelligence Readiness Scale and the Simplified Critical Thinking Scale. Latent profile analysis (LPA) and multinomial logistic regression were performed. Three distinct AI readiness profiles were identified: "Cognition-Deficient Type" (35.6%), "Moderately Balanced Type" (48.0%), and "Comprehensive Excellence Type" (16.4%). Critical thinking scores differed significantly across profiles (p < 0.001), with higher AI readiness associated with stronger critical thinking ability. In terms of other related variables, there were significant differences between the groups in terms of satisfaction with the nursing profession, exposure to AI-medicine interdisciplinary course, attitude towards AI application in healthcare (p < 0.001). Nursing interns exhibit heterogeneous AI readiness levels, which are positively associated with critical thinking. Tailored educational strategies should be developed to enhance both AI readiness and critical thinking skills.

title: Effect of a Breastfeeding Chatbot on Mothers' Breastfeeding Attitudes, Behaviors, and Self-Efficacy
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Adiyaman University; conditions: Breastfeeding, Breastfeeding Attitudes; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 92; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based chatbot developed to address breastfeeding problems on mothers' breastfeeding attitudes, behaviors, and self-efficacy. The study will also assess exclusive breastfeeding rates, breastfeeding duration, and the technical performance and usability of the developed chatbot. The study is planned to include 92 primiparous mothers allocated to intervention and control groups. The intervention involves an AI-based breastfeeding counseling chatbot developed using natural language processing (NLP) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology. The chatbot will provide evidence-based breastfeeding education, information, and counseling support using an expert-reviewed breastfeeding knowledge base. The system is designed to support mothers in managing breastfeeding-related difficulties and will not provide medical diagnoses or replace healthcare professionals. Breastfeeding attitudes, self-efficacy, and behaviors will be evaluated during the postpartum follow-up period. Assessments will be conducted at baseline and at the first, third, and sixth postpartum months. Exclusive breastfeeding rates and breastfeeding duration will also be assessed. Additionally, the chatbot's technical performance, response reliability, medical safety, user satisfaction, and usability will be evaluated. The study aims to provide scientific evidence regarding the effectiveness and feasibility of an AI-supported, evidence-based breastfeeding counseling intervention.

title: Pharmacist-Led Medication Titration for Cardiometabolic Disease: Evidence, Equity, and Scale.
desc: [Current cardiology reports] To review community-based pharmacist-led medication titration across cardiometabolic conditions and the infrastructure needed to deliver this model at scale. This review reframes cardiometabolic medication optimization as a continuum from passive gap identification to active longitudinal medication management. Registries, dashboards, audit and feedback, electronic health record alerts, and inpatient initiation can identify undertreatment or prompt prescribing, but they do not provide infrastructure for dose adjustment, monitoring, adherence support, and medication-access navigation. Pharmacist-led, team-based models occupy the active end of this continuum. The strongest evidence is in hypertension, with meaningful blood pressure reductions; in heart failure, interdisciplinary titration programs more directly address target-dose achievement than alerts or decision-support tools. Emerging data extend this framework to diabetes, lipidology, and obesity. Value-based care provides a reimbursement framework to support these services. Pharmacist-led titration can close gaps between therapies and delivery, but scaling requires equity-focused implementation, flexible staffing, population health infrastructure that connects artificial intelligence-enabled patient identification to action, and sustainable reimbursement.

title: Virtual Human Twins as Tools for Personalized Clinical Care in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: a Pilot Study
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Assistance Publique - Hôpitaux de Paris; conditions: Heart Failure; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 60; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Heart failure (HF) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome characterized by substantial inter-individual variability in pathophysiology and response to treatment. Precision medicine approaches are therefore needed to better account for this heterogeneity and tailor therapeutic strategies to individual patients. Virtual human twins represent one such approach, integrating multimodal clinical, biological, imaging, physiological, and omics data into patient-specific computational models to model disease mechanisms and predict individual therapeutic response. VITAL-HF is a prospective cohort pilot study designed to clinically evaluate the ability of the VITAL cardiovascular virtual human twin to predict individual response to spironolactone in patients with HF. Adult patients with HF with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) \> 40% who have a clinical indication for spironolactone as part of routine care will be enrolled and followed for 3 months. The primary objective is to assess the ability of the VITAL cardiovascular virtual human twin to discriminate responders from non-responders to spironolactone. Response is defined as a ≥20% reduction in NT-proBNP levels 3 months after spironolactone initiation. Virtual twin predictions will be generated for research purposes only and will not influence treatment decisions or patient management.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Detecting Periodontal Diseases Using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography: A Systematic Review.
desc: [Oral diseases] Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have shown promise for the detection of periodontal disease. This study aimed to synthesize current evidence on the diagnostic performance of AI models applied to cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) for periodontal disease. A comprehensive literature search of MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase was conducted to identify studies on AI-assisted diagnosis of periodontal disease using CBCT published up to December 2025. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) tool was used to assess the risk of bias. Among 10,099 records screened, eight studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies indicate that AI models, predominantly based on convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures applied to CBCT images, have substantial potential for detecting periodontal bone loss and related conditions. However, diagnostic performance metrics varied markedly across studies, and direct comparisons with human clinicians produced inconsistent findings, underscoring the need for more rigorous study designs and standardized datasets. Despite limitations arising from heterogeneous methodologies and non-standardized data collection, CBCT-based AI models show considerable promise for enhancing periodontal disease diagnosis. Further high-quality, methodologically robust research is warranted to validate and optimize these approaches for clinical use. PROSPERO: CRD420251273846.

title: Feasibility Study of a Chatbot AI-Driven Preliminary Screening System for Hereditary Cancer Syndromes
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: National Cancer Centre, Singapore; conditions: Hereditary Cancer Syndromes; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 200; status: RECRUITING] This study aims to assess the feasibility of implementing an AI-based hereditary cancer preliminary screening system that has already been developed. This validation cohort will consist of healthy individuals and cancer patients, including those already suspected to be at risk of hereditary conditions.

title: MRI of brain metastases in the era of immunotherapy, targeted agents, and artificial intelligence: from detection to treatment response assessment.
desc: [Magma (New York, N.Y.)] Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to the detection, treatment planning, and response assessment of brain metastases (BM). However, advances in stereotactic radiosurgery, immunotherapy, and targeted therapy have substantially altered the imaging appearance and treatment response patterns of BM, which are not fully captured by conventional imaging and conventional size-based response criteria. This review discusses the evolving role of MRI in BM, from optimized lesion detection to treatment response assessment. We review advanced contrast-enhanced MRI techniques, including three-dimensional turbo spin echo black-blood imaging and post-contrast T2-weighted FLAIR, as well as recent developments in artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted detection. We also examine limitations of RANO-BM and discuss the emerging role of AI-based volumetric analysis for quantitative longitudinal assessment. For differentiating radiation necrosis from tumor progression, we review diffusion and perfusion MRI, MR spectroscopy, and emerging approaches including chemical exchange saturation transfer imaging, radiomics, and tumor habitat analysis. Finally, we highlight how the integration of optimized MRI protocols, multi-parametric imaging, and validated AI-based quantitative tools may improve treatment response assessment and support more precise clinical decision-making for patients with BM.

title: Artificial intelligence in rational drug discovery: optimization of lead compounds and in-silico prediction of molecular interactions for faster pharmaceutical development.
desc: [In silico pharmacology] The conventional drug discovery process is intricate, expensive and time-consuming with high attrition rates. Addressing these inefficiencies has spelled the dawn of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) as game-changers in rational drug design. The review highlights the revolutionary potential of AI techniques such as deep learning and generative models in drug discovery and development. We discuss how AI improves protein-ligand interaction predictions and quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, as well as virtual screening, in drug discovery. In addition, AI can significantly accelerate lead optimization by predicting critical absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties early in the process, allowing for prioritization of promising candidates before time-consuming experimental testing. Although these advancements have been made there still remain several limitations to how broad AI systems are applied in the real world, ranging from data bias and model reliability to the non-interpretability of "black box" neural networks. To overcome these regulatory and ethical challenges, Explainable AI (XAI) must be implemented. In the end, the combination of AI with multi-omics and other technologies such as quantum computing will bring personalized therapy at a much more specific level and significantly shorten the development and research times and costs.

title: Artificial intelligence to support infant feeding and nutritional care: a scoping review.
desc: [Journal of pediatric nursing] Infant feeding and nutrition are critical for growth, development, and long-term health outcomes. As paediatric nurses play a central role in infant monitoring and feeding practices, there is growing interest in innovative approaches to support early assessment and personalised nutritional care. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly explored to support clinical decision-making; however, its applications in infant feeding and nutrition have not been comprehensively synthesised. To map AI applications in infant feeding and nutrition and examine their potential implications for clinical care and paediatric nursing practice. This scoping review followed Arksey and O'Malley's framework and adhered to the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search of research databases was conducted across seven electronic databases, grey literature, and trial registers, including studies published from inception to 26 May 2026. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and extracted and synthesised data. Twenty-nine studies were included. Seven broad AI application areas were identified: 1) prediction and classification of nutritional status, 2) estimation and monitoring of growth, 3) providing nutritional recommendations, 4) analysing nutritional practices and variations, 5) suckling and feeding behaviour analysis, 6) feeding method and behaviour monitoring, and 7) prediction and classification of feeding status. AI demonstrates potential to support paediatric nurses and healthcare professionals by enabling more timely, personalised interventions to improve nutritional care and long-term infant health outcomes. However, current evidence remains largely developmental, highlighting the need for real-world clinical studies to determine the safety, effectiveness, and integration of AI technologies into paediatric care. Open Science Framework (Registration Number: b45tv).

title: Smart livestock management using sensing technologies: applications, digital integration, and future perspectives.
source: PubMed · Tropical animal health and production
desc: [Tropical animal health and production] Smart livestock management is increasingly enabled by advances in sensing and biosensing technologies that support continuous, data-driven monitoring of animal health, welfare, reproduction, productivity, and environmental conditions. Recent digital innovations have further accelerated this transition, creating opportunities for more predictive and sustainable livestock management. This review synthesizes current knowledge on conventional sensors, emerging biosensing technologies, and their integration within smart livestock systems. It critically examines technology readiness, wearable, implantable, and environmental sensing platforms. It evaluates their applications in disease surveillance, animal welfare assessment, reproductive management, milk production optimization, and growth monitoring. The review further explores how the convergence of sensors and biosensors with the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), cloud and edge computing, and digital decision-support systems (DSS) enables continuous data integration, predictive analytics, and evidence-based management. Current barriers to large-scale implementation, including technical reliability, interoperability, data management, infrastructure requirements, economic feasibility, and regulatory and ethical considerations, are also discussed. The available evidence indicates that integrating sensing, biosensing, and digital technologies provides a more comprehensive understanding of animal physiological, behavioral, and environmental status than individual technologies alone, supporting earlier interventions and improved production efficiency. Continued advances in integrated monitoring platforms, intelligent analytics, and next-generation biosensors are expected to accelerate the transition toward predictive, resilient, and sustainable livestock production.

title: Unraveling Structure and Spectroscopic Signatures of Pt/γ-Al2O3 via an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Simulation Framework.
desc: [ACS applied materials & interfaces] Supported subnanometer clusters have attracted significant attention in catalysis. Yet, it is challenging to resolve their structural evolution, particularly in the presence of adsorbates. Here, we present an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled simulation framework that integrates machine learning force field (MLFF) construction, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and ML-assisted infrared (IR) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra analysis to investigate the restructuring of supported subnanometer clusters. Using Pt10/γ-Al2O3(110) as a model system, we explored the CO-induced restructuring of the cluster under different conditions. The simultaneous machine learning (ML)-spectra elucidate a strong interplay among adsorbate coverage, cluster restructuring, and cluster-support interaction. This work sheds light on the complex dynamics of supported subnanometer clusters that is extendible to other systems.

title: The Evolving Landscape of Neonatal Care and Research : Based on 14th Dr. I. C. Verma Excellence in Research Award Delivered as Oration on 4th October 2026.
desc: [Indian journal of pediatrics] Neonatology has undergone a remarkable transformation over the past six decades, evolving from a discipline focused predominantly on preventing neonatal death to one increasingly concerned with quality of survival, neurodevelopment, family-integrated care and long-term health. Despite substantial progress, neonatal mortality remains a major global health challenge. In 2024, approximately 2.3 million newborns died globally, with the highest mortality rates in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. India has achieved a substantial decline in neonatal mortality, from 28 to 17 per 1000 live births between 2015 and 2023, accompanied by rapid expansion of facility-based newborn care. However, prematurity, low birth weight, intrapartum complications, infection, antimicrobial resistance, inequitable access, workforce constraints and inadequate long-term follow-up remain major challenges. The epidemiology of neonatal disease is also changing, with increasing survival of extremely premature infants and greater recognition of bronchopulmonary dysplasia, necrotizing enterocolitis, retinopathy of prematurity, brain injury and developmental impairment. Neonatal research is similarly moving from descriptive epidemiology and rescue therapy towards prediction, prevention, precision medicine and implementation science. The next decade should prioritize prevention of prematurity, precision sepsis management, respiratory and brain protection, nutrition and gut health, Kangaroo Mother Care, zero separation, artificial intelligence and predictive analytics, long-term outcomes and affordable innovations. The ultimate measure of neonatal care should move beyond survival to enabling every newborn to develop and reach their full potential.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Evaluation of Oral Potentially Malignant Disorders Using Photographic and Clinical Data: A Retrospective Exploratory Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
desc: [Dentistry journal] Objective: The objective of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance of GPT-5.2 Thinking in identifying oral potentially malignant disorders within a patient sample that also included oral carcinomas and other oral cavity lesions, using intraoral photographs and associated clinical data. Methods: This retrospective exploratory diagnostic accuracy study included 103 oral lesions: 69 oral potentially malignant disorders, 25 oral carcinomas, and 9 other oral pathologies. Each case was assessed in three independent sessions, and the majority diagnosis was compared with the final clinical and/or histopathological reference diagnosis. Results: For oral potentially malignant disorders, sensitivity was 92.75%, specificity was 88.24%, accuracy was 91.26%, positive predictive value was 94.12%, negative predictive value was 85.71%, and Cohen's kappa was 0.804. Sensitivity was 81.82% for homogeneous leukoplakia, 78.57% for non-homogeneous leukoplakia, and 86.36% for oral lichen planus. For oral carcinomas, sensitivity was 84.00%, specificity was 97.44%, accuracy was 94.17%, positive predictive value was 91.30%, negative predictive value was 95.00%, and Cohen's kappa was 0.837. Conclusions: GPT-5.2 Thinking showed promising diagnostic performance in this exploratory case-enriched dataset, but predictive values require validation in representative clinical populations.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Therapeutic Peptide Discovery and Development.
desc: [Biomolecules] Therapeutic peptides combine biological specificity with chemical versatility, and artificial intelligence (AI) now contributes to their identification, design, and optimisation. Peptide discovery, however, cannot be reduced to generating amino-acid sequences: therapeutic performance also depends on chemistry, conformation, assay context, stability, delivery, safety, manufacturability, and in vivo exposure. This critical review examines AI use across the major peptide classes: receptor agonists, protein-protein interaction inhibitors, oncology and tumour-targeting peptides, antimicrobial and phenotype-driven peptides, delivery peptides, vaccine epitopes, self-assembling materials, and chemically constrained macrocycles. It compares sequence-based, chemical, graph, structure-aware, and multimodal representations across predictive, generative, and experimentally integrated workflows. Coverage spans recent general protein foundation, prediction, and design systems (ProtGPT2, ESM-2/ESM3, ProGen/ProGen2, ProteinMPNN, RFdiffusion, and AlphaFold 3) and peptide-focused methods (RFpeptides, PepFlow, and PepGLAD). Particular attention is given to benchmark integrity, the limits of structure prediction for short and non-canonical molecules, and the gap between retrospective and prospective evidence. To make claims comparable, the review adapts established reporting, validation, and readiness concepts into a peptide-specific, two-dimensional Peptide-AI Evidence Grid that separates methodological rigour (M0-M3) from translational depth (T0-T3), applies it to representative studies, and provides a checklist extending DOME, TRIPOD + AI, and FAIR guidance with the chemistry- and assay-specific items peptide work requires.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Purposes of Public Health: A Critical Look at Technology.
desc: [The Hastings Center report] Within public health, the contemporary discourse surrounding AI in this field is dominated by what this paper terms the "standard approach." In this frame, AI appears as a neutral tool to be evaluated for accuracy, privacy protection, and bias mitigation. When direct benefits outweigh direct harms, AI is described as an opportunity to improve public health practice. But the standard approach does not consider how public health's adoption of AI discloses and reinforces different accounts of the underlying purpose of the profession. Drawing insights from the communitarian thinker Wendell Berry, we demonstrate how AI does not merely improve efficiency and add capabilities but tends to align public health practice with purposes and assumptions that, when actualized, increasingly displace community power and authentic human presence. This tendency is clear in three commonly proposed applications of AI in public health practice: health education, community health assessments, and data analysis. Because the advent of AI offers an opportunity for greater technological efficiency, it offers the public health community the opportunity to reflect on what ultimate ends those efficiencies should be directed toward.

title: Transglycosidases from aspergillus genus and their applications in food processing: Advances in enzyme mining and smart biocatalysis.
source: PubMed · International journal of biological macromolecules
desc: [International journal of biological macromolecules] Transglycosidases (TGs) constitute a family of glycoside hydrolases that perform glycosyl transfer via intra- and intermolecular substitution. A. niger, A. oryzae, and other Aspergillus strains represent the major industrial sources of TGs, which are widely applied in food processing. However, prominent bottlenecks still restrict the optimization of enzyme performance, industrial adaptation, and the construction of synergistic catalytic systems. This comprehensive review expounds the application potential of Aspergillus-derived TGs in food processing, analyzes the scientific basis of artificial intelligence (AI) regulation on enzyme catalytic performance, systematically summarizes the molecular modification and multi-enzyme synergistic mechanisms, and illustrates their application effects in the fields of prebiotic oligosaccharides, dairy products, brewing, and baking. Furthermore, it promotes the in-depth integration of AI and food biomanufacturing, and advances the high-quality development of the green functional food processing industry, showing sustainable and bright prospects in smart bioprocessing and big-health food research.

title: Multimodal artificial intelligence assessment of simulated cardiac arrest performance: a pilot study.
desc: [Resuscitation plus] Assessment of simulated cardiac arrest performance is resource-intensive and subject to inter-rater variability. We evaluated whether a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) system could score video-recorded cardiac arrest megacode simulations with agreement comparable to expert raters. Six scripted megacode simulations (three ventricular fibrillation, three pulseless electrical activity) representing exemplar, guideline-deviation and non-technical-deficiency performance were scored by two ACLS instructors using a validated team-leader checklist; consensus ratings served as the reference. Two operators analysed each video with Gemini 1.5 Pro at three temperature settings (504 item-level ratings). We calculated Cohen's kappa, Gwet's AC1, and sensitivity and specificity for identifying performed and omitted actions, and compared AI self-reported confidence between correct and incorrect ratings. Expert inter-rater agreement was κ = 0.78 (95% CI 0.64-0.93). AI-expert agreement was κ = 0.62 (95% CI 0.49-0.75; range 0.40-0.86 across configurations) and AC1 = 0.77. The AI identified performed actions with high sensitivity (0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99) but detected omitted actions poorly (specificity 0.58, 95% CI 0.44-0.72), particularly omissions defined by timing or sequence. Temperature had no consistent effect. Incorrect ratings of actions as performed carried lower mean self-reported confidence than correct ones (93.6 vs 98.1), but 48% were made with maximal confidence. A multimodal AI system reliably confirmed completed actions but frequently failed to detect omitted actions, yielding moderate overall agreement that was below expert-expert agreement. Current systems may support, but not replace, expert assessment of cardiac arrest simulation.

title: Any Artificial Intelligence Tool Use Experience and Depression-Anxiety Symptom Profiles Among Rural University Students in China.
source: PubMed · Psychology research and behavior management
desc: [Psychology research and behavior management] Associations of artificial intelligence (AI) tool use with concurrent depressive and anxiety symptoms among rural university students remain uncertain. We explored associations of any AI tool use experience with depression-anxiety symptom profiles. This cross-sectional survey included 1529 students with rural household registration from three universities in Zhejiang, China. GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scores informed latent profile analysis; five conceptually ordered multinomial models compared profile membership with the low-symptom profile. The profiles comprised low symptoms (n=896; 58.6%), anxiety-predominant symptoms (n=587; 38.4%), and depression-predominant symptoms (n=46; 3.0%). In the reported fully adjusted model, AI use experience was associated with lower odds of anxiety-predominant membership (OR=0.764, 95% CI 0.654-0.893) and depression-predominant membership (OR=0.239, 95% CI 0.101-0.566) compared with low-symptom membership. AI use experience and symptom patterns were associated in this exploratory sample. These observations warrant longitudinal assessment with more detailed measures of AI engagement.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Employee Innovation: A Literature Review.
desc: [Behavioral sciences (Basel, Switzerland)] Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is increasingly embedded in knowledge work, creative work, customer service, product development, human resource management, and organizational decision systems. Although research shows that AI can raise productivity, support creative output, accelerate searching, and reorganize innovation work, the evidence remains fragmented across innovation management, organizational behavior, information systems, human resource management, economics, human-computer interaction, and behavioral sciences. This framework-based review synthesizes high-quality English-language journal articles on AI, human-AI collaboration, employee creativity, innovative work behavior, algorithmic management, and innovation management. Building on established models of individual innovation, it develops a worker-centered framework linking four innovation stages with three higher-order AI functions: task execution, knowledge support, and organizational governance. The evidence is strongest for searching, idea generation, creativity, and short-term task performance, and remains limited for idea promotion, implementation, diffusion, and realized innovation outcomes. The synthesis identifies three central tensions: performance equalization versus capability differentiation, short-term quality versus long-term capability development, and individual improvement versus collective homogenization. AI can enhance innovation-related work through cognitive expansion, search acceleration, productivity release, recombination, feedback, and learning, but it can also reduce output diversity, weaken expertise development, intensify work, increase dependence, and shift managerial control over creative labor. The review positions AI as both a cognitive resource and an innovation-governance mechanism and outlines directions for future research on mechanisms, heterogeneity, novelty, capability accumulation, and responsible governance.
